display.purpose: Page-level h1 headlines; italic spans carry the Assay Copper Bright emphasis color.

body.purpose: Intro paragraphs and body copy; max-width 66ch.

label.purpose: Nav links, buttons, footer headings, breadcrumbs — anything functioning as metadata or navigation.

eyebrow.purpose: Signature small-caps kicker above headlines, preceded by a 34px hairline.

shadows.name: card-rest
shadows.purpose: Default ambient elevation for primary buttons and cards at rest (The Raised-Ore Rule).

shadows.name: card-hover
shadows.purpose: Copper-tinted lift on hover/focus for primary buttons and cards, paired with translateY(-4px).

shadows.name: error-glow
shadows.purpose: Semantic-only invalid form field state; never used decoratively.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default transition for hover/focus state changes on cards, nav, and links.

components.name: Nav Button

narrative.overview:
MineTrans's marketing and training surfaces read like a certified assay report on a valuable metal: dark, precise, evidentiary. The onyx-black canvas and thin hairline rules are the paper of a technical document; Playfair Display headlines are the authoritative typeset title; Jost's uppercase, wide-tracked small-caps labels are the stamped, measured annotations along the margin; Inter body copy is the plain explanatory prose underneath. Assay Copper is the one warm material in the system — it appears sparingly, the way a seal or a highlighted figure would on a real report, never as decoration.

This is a Persuade surface (the marketing site) built with the discipline of an Operate surface: nothing performs looseness or informality. The system currently exists fully realized only in client/public/*.html (the static marketing pages). The certification portal and the shadcn/ui component library run an unrelated generic blue-on-white / slate-amber theme — this is confirmed drift, not a second intentional world. Do not treat the portal's current look as a design reference; it is the thing that needs to converge onto this system.
keyCharacteristics: Onyx-black canvas with a single warm accent (copper), never a busy palette.
Editorial serif display type over engraved small-caps labels; body text stays quiet.
Flat, hairline-bordered surfaces as the base language — with one confirmed exception: primary buttons and cards now carry real shadow/lift, not just a border.
Near-square geometry (2-4px radii) throughout; nothing rounded or soft.
Numbers and named steps (12-step methodology, 18-category questionnaire) are treated as first-class content, not buried in prose.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Copper is the only saturated color in the system. If a second accent hue is needed for a state, it must be semantic, never decorative.

rules.name: The Semantic Red Exception
rules.body: Validation/error states use a separate red glow — this is a state color, not a palette option; it never appears outside form validation.

rules.name: The Stamped Label Rule
rules.body: Anything that reads as metadata or navigation is Jost, uppercase, letter-spaced. Any Playfair Display text is a title, never a label.

rules.name: The Raised-Ore Rule
rules.body: Primary buttons and cards are never perfectly flat. A hairline border alone is no longer sufficient — they carry ambient shadow at rest and a copper-tinted lift on interaction. Every other surface stays flat by design.

dos: Do keep copper to eyebrows, CTAs, hover states, and single accent strokes — per The One Accent Rule.
Do give primary buttons and cards real shadow now (ambient at rest, copper glow on hover) — per The Raised-Ore Rule.
Do use Jost uppercase small-caps for anything that functions as a label, metadata, or navigation; reserve Playfair Display for titles.
Do keep nav, footer, content blocks, and section chrome flat with hairline borders — the elevation upgrade is scoped to buttons and cards only.
Do treat the 12-step BI methodology and 18-category questionnaire as first-class, numbered content.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue outside the confirmed semantic red for validation errors.
Don't round corners beyond the established 2-4px scale; large/soft radii are off-brand.
Don't treat the certification portal's current slate/amber shadcn theme as a design reference — it is confirmed drift from this system, not an alternate world.
Don't add shadow/elevation to nav, footer, or content blocks (.block) — the Raised-Ore Rule is scoped to buttons and cards.
